Subject: Orion Signal pilot: quick ask on GPU provisioning readiness

Hi team,

Late-stage update on the Orion Signal pilot (HS-ORION-778). They indicated a firm go/no-go window of ~4–6 weeks and want capacity assurances tied to a signed commitment. Can you run a short readiness check for dedicated GPU availability in us-west-2 and outline options for a provisional hold?

Details from PD: pilot will need an initial 8 concurrent A100-style GPUs for a 6-week POC with expected 12M tokens/day at peak. They'd prefer dedicated nodes but are open to a burst model if we can guarantee latency SLOs.

Ask:
- karthik: can you inventory available dedicated capacity and potential backfill impact?
- aditya: costs/ops implications and recommended hold window (soft hold vs formal reserve).
- marissa: I may need you to loop procurement on timing if we recommend a hold.

Attached: Orion_MA_plan.pdf (one-page mutual action plan).

Thanks,
Markus Klein
Head of Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference

[Attachment: Orion_MA_plan.pdf (PDF, 1 page)]

Markus —

Thanks for the heads-up. Quick inventory: in us-west-2 we currently have the following uncommitted pool that could be used for Dedicated/Dedicated-reserved assignments:
- 12 x A100S-equivalent on dedicated clusters (idle capacity but some are earmarked for other committed customers with flexible start dates)
- 20 x T4/GPU-class on burst nodes (not ideal for sustained throughput but OK for short POCs)

Constraints/risks:
- If we allocate 8 A100s from the dedicated pool, we reduce our schedule flexibility for other near-term renewals — we'd need a backfill plan if another committed customer asks for immediate scale.
- Kernel optimization for their model suggests sustained memory pressure; A100-class is recommended.

Recommendation: create a provisional (soft) hold on 8 A100s for 30 days, with an explicit expiration and an ops playbook that allows us to reclaim with 7 days notice if a higher-priority SLA-bound customer requires them. If Orion signs in the 30-day window, we convert to a formal Dedicated reservation.

I'll tag the candidate hosts and open a REQ ticket with infra.

—Karthik
Senior Capacity Planner
Redwood Inference

Markus / Karthik —

I ran a short ops impact analysis. Key points:
- Cost/ops: Holding 8 A100-class for 30 days (soft hold) carries an opportunity cost ~ $36k equivalent in billable hours if we ultimately reassign; converting to Reserved Dedicated reduces unit cost by ~20% but requires a minimum 3-month commitment.
- Backfill: we can mitigate by enabling burst overlap for low-priority workloads on non-critical nodes and scheduling maintenance windows to free capacity if needed.
- SLA surface: if we grant a soft hold with a 7-day reclaim policy, we should include that explicitly in our communications.

Operational recommendation (preferred):
1) Create provisional soft hold for 8 A100s in us-west-2 for 30 days (expiry 2027-09-11) and link REQ-4521 to track changes.
2) Offer Orion a 10-business-day exclusive negotiation window to convert to a Dedicated reservation; during that window we will not reassign their held nodes unless they breach the negotiation terms.
3) Provide a short addendum that spells out reclaim policy and expected costs if they convert later.

I've attached our internal hold_policy.md stub for reference. If legal/product wants a different wording for the exclusive window, let me know.

Aditya Rao
Director, Capacity Ops
Redwood Inference

[Attachment: hold_policy.md (text, 2 pages)]

Confirmed: based on recommendations from capacity and ops, we have placed a provisional soft hold for 8 A100-class GPUs in us-west-2. Details below:
- Hold ID: REQ-4521 (see ticket)
- Hold window: 2027-08-15 through 2027-09-11 (30-day soft hold)

- Day-of cutover ops contact: ops-oncall@redwood.com (primary: Karthik Iyer)
